title: Teen Tennis Player Scores a Surprise First Win
summary:
British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic has won her first WTA Tour main-draw match — and she only found out she was playing one hour before it started!

The 17-year-old had lost in qualifying for the Hong Kong Open. But another player pulled out, so Stojsavljevic got a second chance as a "lucky loser."

Her opponent was Sofia Kenin, a former Australian Open champion ranked 224 places above her. Stojsavljevic won the match 6-3, 4-6, 6-4.

"I only knew an hour before I was going to be playing. I kind of just went out and swung today," she said. "I believed in myself and it worked out."

Stojsavljevic started playing tennis at age seven in London. In 2024, she won the US Open junior title — the first Briton in 15 years to do it.

Next, she plays world number 67 Zeynep Sonmez in the second round.
why_it_matters: Mika's win shows that being ready when a surprise chance comes — and believing in yourself — can change everything, even at 17.
